action: General advice: if you run refrigeration or building controllers, keep their management interfaces off the internet and keep a manual plan for moving stock if cooling fails.
actor: Shahid Kaveh (IRGC-linked), per French authorities as reported by The Register and Ynetnews
exec: France is taking a sabotage cyber campaign against refrigeration controllers to a diplomatic level, with EU sanctions to be sought, Barrot said.
impact: Refrigeration controllers were attacked in France; per Ynetnews, French blood bank cold storage was disrupted in a November wave.
org: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
plain: France says it will seek EU sanctions over the attacks that disrupted supermarket refrigeration controllers. The Register and Ynetnews report French authorities blame an IRGC-linked unit; Iran rejects the accusations, Semana reports.

key_findings: In a November 10 interview published by the ministry, Jean-Noel Barrot called the refrigeration attack unprecedented in scale and aggressiveness and the first sabotage cyberattack of that size.
He said he would summon Iran's ambassador to convey France's protest.
He said France will seek EU sanctions on those responsible, meaning entry bans and asset freezes, as early as possible.
He said further proportionate measures would follow, some of which would not be made public.
He did not name the unit himself and declined to say whether Iran is behind other recent cyberattacks, citing ongoing investigations.
report.publisher: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
recommendations: The interview contains no guidance for organisations.

sources.name: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (France Info interview, 10 November 2026)

summary: Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on November 10 that France will seek EU sanctions on those responsible for the refrigeration-controller attacks and will summon Iran’s ambassador. The Register and Ynetnews report that French authorities blame the IRGC-linked unit Shahid Kaveh; Ynetnews adds Paris prosecutors requested arrest warrants. Semana reports Iran’s Foreign Ministry rejected the accusations as unfounded and unilateral.
title: France to seek EU sanctions over refrigeration-controller sabotage and summon Iran’s ambassador

validation.note: Corroborated by the ministry’s own interview (sanctions, ambassador) and independent publishers The Register and Ynetnews (attribution to Shahid Kaveh). Arrest warrants rest on Ynetnews only; Iran’s rejection on Semana only.

review.note: date (16 to 10 Nov, interview date), title no longer names IRGC as sanctions target, unsourced impact claims removed, attribution tied to Register/Ynetnews, action marked general advice, validation note, published days

date_note: Day of Barrot’s France Info interview on the ministry page; the earlier attacks and Register’s 9 November report are not the sanctions announcement.
